how_this_was_recorded: Built from the repository at commit 1b44ebf with ./mvnw package, then started with:
TALLY_DB_URL was left unset, so the server ran on its in-memory store and touched no database.
Every request below was made with curl. Every response body and status line is copied verbatim.
Account ids, the transfer id and the timestamps are the real ones the server generated in that run.
world_account_note: world is the reserved account the service uses to fund opening balances. It is the only account allowed to hold a negative balance, and its balance is the negative of every dollar ever issued, which is why the whole book adds up to zero. Source: src/main/java/dev/tally/core/WorldAccount.java

steps.heading: Open two accounts
steps.plain: Amara opens an account with 500.00 in it. Ben opens an empty one.
steps.bookNote: The 500.00 was moved out of world, not typed in.
steps.caption: Amara's opening 500.00 was not conjured up. It was moved out of an account called world, so the book already adds up to zero.

steps.heading: Ask for the balances
steps.plain: This is the starting point everything after it is measured against.
steps.caption: Amara has 500.00 and Ben has nothing. Balances are counted in whole cents, never in decimals, so there is nothing to round.

steps.heading: Amara sends Ben 125.00
steps.plain: The client attaches a label it made up for this one payment.
steps.bookNote: Minus 125.00 on one side, plus 125.00 on the other.
steps.caption: One payment wrote two entries that cancel out. Amara is down 125.00, Ben is up 125.00, and the book still adds up to zero.

steps.heading: The reply gets lost, so the client sends it again
steps.plain: Exactly the same request, byte for byte, including the same key.
steps.bookNote: Not one cent different from the step before.
steps.caption: Same answer, same payment number, and a header saying this was a repeat. The money moved once, not twice.

steps.heading: Check the balances again
steps.plain: Two requests went out. Count how many payments landed.
steps.caption: Ben got 125.00 once, although the request arrived twice. Amara is down 125.00 once, for the same reason.

steps.heading: Ben tries to send 9,000.00 he does not have
steps.plain: He holds 125.00. He asks to move 9,000.00.
steps.bookNote: Nothing moved. The bars are the ones from the step before.
steps.caption: Refused, with the reason and both numbers in the open. Nothing was written down, so there is nothing to clean up later.

steps.heading: Balances after the refusal
steps.plain: A refusal has to leave the money exactly where it was.
steps.bookNote: Identical to two steps ago, to the cent.
steps.caption: The same two numbers as before the refusal. A refused payment is not a partly done payment.

steps.heading: Audit the whole book
steps.plain: The service re-adds every entry it ever wrote.
steps.bookNote: 375.00 plus 125.00 above the line, 500.00 below it. Difference: 0.
steps.caption: Three accounts checked, no disagreements, and every balance adds up to exactly zero. Checked on demand, not assumed.

steps.heading: Read Ben's statement
steps.plain: One line per movement, with the balance immediately after it.
steps.bookNote: One entry for Ben, because one payment reached him.
steps.caption: One line: 125.00 in, from Amara, leaving 125.00. The repeat in step 4 never became a second payment, so it left no line.

unauthorised_write.note: A separate request in the same recorded run, with the Authorization header left off entirely.
